Surah 51: al-Dhariyat (The Scattering Winds) [Meccan, and its verses are sixty]

﴿By the scatterers, scattering﴾: the winds that scatter the dust and other things. ﴿Scattering﴾ is a verbal noun (masdar); it is also said: "tadhrīhi dharyan," meaning it blows it about.

Quranic quotations are between ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translate the passage.

﴿Then those that carry the burden﴾ — the clouds, which carry the water. ﴿A load﴾ — a weight; it is the object (maf'ul) of "those that carry."

Translation:

﴿Then those that run﴾ the ships that glide over the surface of the water ﴿with ease﴾, an infinitive (maṣdar) in the position of a circumstantial state (ḥāl), meaning facilitated/made easy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 4:

﴿Then by those who distribute by command﴾ The angels who distribute provisions, rain, and other things among the lands and the servants.

﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾: *mā* is *maṣdariyyah* (the particle that turns the following words into a verbal noun), meaning their promise of the resurrection and other things, ﴿is surely true﴾, a true promise.
The Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And indeed, the Recompense﴾ — the reward after the reckoning ﴿is surely to come﴾ without doubt.
﴿By the sky, full of paths﴾. Ḥubuk is the plural of ḥabīka, like ṭarīqa and ṭarīq; i.e., possessing paths in its creation, like the paths in sand.

Indeed you (O people of Makkah) are in a discordant opinion concerning the Prophet ﷺ and the Qur'an, ﴿in a discordant saying﴾. It has been said: (they say he is a) poet, a magician, a soothsayer; (it is) poetry, magic, soothsaying.

﴿Is turned away﴾ means is turned aside ﴿from it﴾, from the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, that is, from belief in it. ﴿Whoever is turned away﴾ means is turned aside from guidance in the knowledge of God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 10:

﴿Cursed be the conjecturers﴾ (qutila al-kharrasun): cursed be the liars, the people of the contradictory speech.

Those who are in a heedless state: ignorance that overwhelms them, and they are unmindful, heedless of the matter of the Hereafter.

Wait, I need to correct that: the translation should render the Qur'anic quotation with its markers and keep the technical structure. Here is the faithful translation:

﴿Those who are in heedlessness﴾: ignorance that overwhelms them, ﴿heedless﴾: unmindful of the matter of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 12:

﴿They ask﴾ the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mocking question, ﴿"When is the Day of Judgment?"﴾ i.e., when will it come? Their answer is: "It will come."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 51, verse 13:

﴿On the Day they will be tormented over the Fire﴾, i.e., they will be punished therein, and it will be said to them at the time of punishment:

﴿Taste your trial⦆ — your punishment — ﴿this, which you used to hasten⦆ — in this world, mockingly.

Translation note: the passage gives the gloss of the Qur'anic words in brackets-free form as follows.

﴿Taste your trial﴾ (i.e., your punishment) ﴿this [punishment] which you used to hasten﴾ (in the world, mockingly).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens﴾ (i.e., orchards) ﴿and springs﴾ flowing within them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 16:

﴿Receiving﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in the predicate of inna (indeed), ﴿what their Lord has given them﴾ meaning, He has bestowed upon them, ﴿of reward﴾. ﴿Indeed they were before that﴾ i.e., before their entry into Paradise, ﴿good-doers﴾ in the worldly life.

﴿They used to sleep but little of the night.﴾ *Yanamun* (they sleep). *Ma* is an extra particle (*za'ida*). *Yahja'un* is the predicate (*khabar*) of *kana*, and *qalilan* is an adverbial of time (*zarf*, adverb of time or place), meaning: they would sleep for a short time of the night, and they would pray most of it.

And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness (of Allah).

Commentary: "And in the hours before dawn (ṣaḥar) they would ask forgiveness" — the verse ﴿And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness﴾. They would say: "O Allah, forgive us."
﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived.﴾ [The deprived is] the one who does not ask because of his self-restraint.

Surah 51, verse 20 in the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn):

﴿And on the earth﴾ — from mountains, seas, trees, fruits, plants and other things — ﴿are signs﴾, i.e., indications of the power of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and of His oneness.

"And in yourselves [are signs also], from the beginning of your creation to its end, and in the wonders of the composition of your creation. ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ That, so that you might infer from it the existence of its Maker and His power."
﴿وفِي السَّماء رِزْقكُمْ﴾ i.e., the rain, from which the plants grow, which is provision ﴿وما تُوعَدُونَ﴾ of the return, the reward and the punishment; i.e., that is written in the heaven.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 23:

﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it﴾ i.e., what you are promised ﴿is certainly true, just as it is true that you speak﴾. The word "mithl" (just like) is in the nominative (raf') as an adjective, and "mā" is extra (ziyadah); it is also read with a fatha on the lām, in which case "mithl" is compounded (murakkabah) with "mā". The meaning is: "like your speech" in its reality, i.e., its being known to you, the necessity of its issuing from you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 24:

﴿Has there come to you﴾ an address to the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿the story of Abraham's honored guests?﴾ They were angels, twelve or ten or three, among them Jibril (Gabriel).

﴿إذْ﴾ is an adverbial of time (ظَرْف, ẓarf) that modifies the account of the guest: ﴿دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقالُوا سَلامًا﴾ ("when they entered upon him and said, 'Peace'"), meaning this utterance. ﴿قالَ سَلام﴾ ("He said, 'Peace'"), meaning this utterance. ﴿قَوْم مُنْكَرُونَ﴾ ("a people unknown"), meaning: "We do not know you." He said this to himself. It is the predicate (خَبَر, khabar) of an omitted subject (مُبْتَدَأ, mubtada'), meaning: "These are a people unknown."
﴿Then he turned﴾ away, going secretly ﴿to his household﴾, ﴿and brought a fat calf﴾. In Surah Hud it is ﴿a roasted calf﴾, i.e., broiled.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 27:

﴿So he brought it near to them. He said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ He offered them the food, but they did not respond.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 28:

﴿So he conceived fear of them in himself﴾ (fa-awjasa) he concealed within himself ﴿of them﴾, ﴿fear﴾. ﴿They said: "Do not fear."﴾ ﴿We are messengers of your Lord.﴾ ﴿And they gave him good tidings of a boy endowed with knowledge﴾, one of abundant knowledge, and he was Isaac, as was mentioned in Hud.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 29:

﴿Then his wife came forward﴾ Sarah, ﴿crying out﴾ a cry, as a circumstantial state; meaning she came crying out. ﴿And she struck her face﴾ she slapped it, ﴿and said: An old woman, barren!﴾ who had never given birth, and her age was ninety-nine years, while the age of Ibrahim was one hundred years; or his age was one hundred and twenty years, and her age was ninety years.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 30:

﴿They said: "Thus," i.e., like our statement concerning the glad tidings, "Your Lord has said: Indeed, He is the All-Wise" in His creation, "the All-Knowing" of His creatures.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 31:

﴿Said, "Then what is your business?"﴾ (shanukum): i.e., what is your affair?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 32:

﴿They said: "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals"﴾ — disbelievers; they are the people of Lut.
To send down upon them stones of clay, baked by fire.

[Mu­sawwamah] marked, on it being the name of the one at whom it is to be hurled. [ʿInda rabbika] is an adverbial complement (ẓarf) of it. [Lil-musrifin] for those who commit excess (al-musrifun), by their coming to males together with their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 35:

﴿So We brought out whoever was in it﴾, i.e., the towns of the people of Lut, ﴿of the believers﴾, [and this was] for the destruction of the disbelievers.

Translation:

﴿So We found not therein any house of the Muslims [in submission to Allah]﴾. They are Lut and his two daughters, who were described with faith (iman) and submission (islam), meaning they affirm with their hearts and act with their limbs in obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 37:

﴿And We left therein﴾ after the destruction of the disbelievers ﴿a sign﴾ an indication of their destruction ﴿for those who fear the painful punishment﴾ so that they do not do the like of their deeds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 38:

﴿And in Musa (Moses)﴾ is coordinated (ma'tuf) with "fiha" (in it), the meaning being: and We placed in the story of Musa a sign, ﴿when We sent him to Fir'awn (Pharaoh)﴾ accompanied by ﴿clear authority﴾, that is, with a manifest proof.

﴿So he turned away﴾, meaning he turned away from belief, ﴿with his power﴾, meaning with his soldiers, because they were to him like a pillar of support. ﴿And said﴾ of Moses, ﴿"He is a sorcerer or a madman"﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 40:

﴿So We seized him and his hosts, and cast them into the sea﴾ — i.e., We threw them — ﴿into the sea﴾ — the sea (al-yamm), meaning the sea (al-bahr) — so they drowned, ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾ — i.e., Pharaoh, who had committed that for which he was to be blamed, namely denying the messengers and claiming lordship (al-rububiyyah).

And in the destruction of ʿĀd there is a sign, when We sent upon them the barren wind (ﷺ not applicable) ...

Let me restate cleanly:

And in the destruction of ʿĀd there is a sign ﴿when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ — the one in which there is no good, because it does not carry rain and does not fertilize trees; and it is the dabūr (the west wind).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 42:

﴿It leaves nothing it comes upon but makes it like rottenness﴾ [i.e., a person or property] ﴿It leaves nothing it comes upon but makes it like rottenness﴾ [i.e., like that which is decayed and crumbled to pieces].

﴿And in﴾ the destruction of ﴿Thamud﴾ is a sign, ﴿when it was said to them﴾, after the slaughter of the she-camel, ﴿"Enjoy yourselves for a time."﴾ That is, until the end of your lifespans, as in another verse.

﴿So they were arrogant﴾ [and] ﴿against the command of their Lord﴾, i.e., in refusing to comply with it. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾ after three days had passed, i.e., the destructive cry, ﴿while they were looking on﴾, i.e., during the daytime.
﴿So they were not able to stand up﴾, meaning they were not able to rise when the punishment descended, ﴿nor were they ones who could defend themselves﴾ against those who destroyed them.

﴿And the people of Noah﴾ with *بِالجَرِّ* (in the genitive) is conjoined to *ثَمُود* (Thamud), meaning: and in their destruction by what is in the heavens and the earth is a sign. With *بِالنَّصْبِ* (in the accusative), it means: and We destroyed the people of Noah ﴿from before﴾, meaning: before the destruction of those mentioned.

﴿And the heaven We built with might﴾ (bi-quwwah), ﴿and indeed We are its expanders﴾ (qadirun), meaning capable. It is said: *ada al-rajul ya'idu* (ﺁﺩ ﺍﻟﺮﺟﻞ ﻳﺌﻴﺪ), meaning he became strong, and *awsa'a al-rajul* (ﺃﻭﺳﻊ ﺍﻟﺮﺟﻞ), meaning he became one possessing abundance and strength.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 48:

﴿And the earth – We spread it out, so excellent are the spreaders﴾ – We made it a bed (mahhadnaha), ﴿so excellent are the spreaders﴾ – We (nahnu).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 49:

﴿And of everything﴾ is related to His saying: ﴿We created﴾ ﴿pairs﴾, two kinds, such as the male and the female, the heaven and the earth, the sun and the moon, the plain and the mountain, summer and winter, the sweet and the sour, the light and the darkness. ﴿So that you may remember﴾: with one of the two tā' elided from the original, so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One, and worship Him.
﴿So flee to Allah﴾, i.e., to His reward from His punishment, by obeying Him and not disobeying Him. ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾, clear in the warning.

﴿Do not set up with Allah another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾

The phrase قُلْ لَهُمْ (say to them) is to be understood as supplied before فَفِرُّوا (so flee).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 51, verse 52:

﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them without their saying, "He is a sorcerer or a madman."﴾ That is, their denial of you, in saying that you are a sorcerer or a madman, is like the denial of the nations before them of their messengers, in their saying that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 51, verse 53:

﴿Did they enjoin it upon one another?﴾ — all of them: an interrogative used in the sense of negation (istifham bi-ma'na al-nafy). ﴿Nay, they are a transgressing people.﴾ Their transgression (tughyan) brought them together upon this statement.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 54:

﴿So turn away from them﴾ (aʿriḍ, "turn away from") ʿanhum, ﴿for you are not to be blamed﴾ because you have conveyed the message to them.
﴿And remind﴾, admonish with the Qur'an, ﴿for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾, those whom God, exalted is He, knows will believe.

And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me (﴿Qur'an 51:56﴾). This does not contradict the fact that the disbelievers do not worship, because the purpose (al-ghayah) does not necessarily have to exist, as in your saying: "I sharpened this pen so that I may write with it," though you may not actually write with it.
﴿I do not desire any provision from them﴾ for Myself, nor for themselves or for others, ﴿nor do I desire that they feed Me﴾, nor themselves, nor others.
﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ *Al-Shadid* (the Severe).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 51, verse 59:

﴿Indeed, for those who wronged﴾ themselves through disbelief, from among the people of Makkah and others, ﴿a portion﴾, meaning a share of the punishment, ﴿like the portion﴾, meaning the share, ﴿of their companions﴾, meaning those destroyed before them, ﴿so let them not seek to hasten﴾ the punishment, even though I delay it for them until the Day of Resurrection.
﴿Fa-waylun﴾ (woe), meaning severe punishment, ﴿for those who disbelieve, from﴾ [i.e., in] ﴿their Day which they are promised﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection.
